sources.title: Inversions in parking functions
proof_comparison_scope: Sections 2-3: forest bijection, symmetric function, stable principal specialization
Section 4: unit interval block structure, Cayley bijection, inversion q-EGF
Section 5: k-transitive expectation theorem and applications
Bradt et al. 2024 Theorem 2.9 published PDF pages 6-7

local_defects.finding: false for sorted UPF 11 at i=2; intended form appears to be a'_i in {i-1,i}
local_defects.impact: subsequent Cayley bijection uses block order and sizes, not the false clause

relevance.foothold: Sn-invariance condition holds for PF_n, but a useful Theorem 5.2 application would additionally need a small fixed-k positional-sum representation of maximum displacement; the paper provides none

sources.title: Counting l-interval Fubini rankings through their parking outcome
proof_comparison_scope: Sections 2-4: ordered set partition flattening, run decomposition, Fibonacci/Pingala product
Aguilar-Fraga et al. 2024 Theorems 4.15-4.16 and surrounding proof
dependency_findings: cites S2 Theorem 4.16 only; does not cite or repair S2 Theorems 4.1 or 4.14
correctly restricts the Fibonacci count to weakly increasing/identity-outcome unit Fubini rankings and states total UFR_3=12, correcting the scope of S2 Theorem 4.15
for Fubini rankings, tie-block maximum size <= l+1 is equivalent to maximum displacement <= l

local_defects.finding: Fibonacci seeds are printed once as F1=F2=1 but the theorem and Pingala definition use the shifted convention F1=1,F2=2
one product prints 2^(c1-1), while statement (18) and calculation use 2^(ci-1)

relevance.foothold: strongest new foothold: fixed-outcome maximum-displacement bound factorizes by increasing runs inside the Fubini-ranking subfamily only

sources.title: Luck and magic for Pitman-Stanley polytopes and parking functions
proof_comparison_scope: Theorems 1.1-1.2: magic positivity and h-star real-rootedness consequence
Sections 3-4: block/classical parking protocols, lucky statistic, dominance-preserving algorithm and double count

relevance.foothold: comparison template for transferring coefficient properties through an exact linear transformation; the paper provides no such link for maximum displacement

sources.title: Parking functions, Smirnov words, and noncrossing Chow polynomials
proof_comparison_scope: Sections 3-4: multiplicity-type transfer and last-letter interlacing
Sections 5-7: peak/tie insertion, Narayana refinement, full descent distribution
Sections 8-9 and Appendices A-B: toric contributions, image size, pattern classes, independent real-rootedness proofs
real_rooted_targets: toric g contributions and nonnegative row sums

relevance.foothold: finite refinement plus interlacing is a methodological template, but its states and transfers do not preserve maximum displacement
